module.name: Structural_Love
module.author: TriadicFrameworks Core
module.description: Formalizes love as a structural property of a relational system, defined by the measurable configuration of four operators (COHE, PRI, BOND, CARE) acting across a triadic alignment of Self, Other, and System.
module.key_claim: Love is not a cause of relational stability — it is structural stability, expressed at the operator level.

triadic_nodes.label: Self
triadic_nodes.role: Source of PRI allocation; CARE activation origin; internal COHE model

triadic_nodes.label: Other
triadic_nodes.role: Target of CARE; object of COHE modeling; co-author of BOND

triadic_nodes.label: System
triadic_nodes.role: Container for BOND; the medium through which all operator signals travel

operators.name: Coherence Operator
operators.measures: Degree to which each agent's internal model of the other is consistent, updated, and integrated
operators.failure_mode: Phantom bonding — agent relates to a representation rather than the actual other
operators.recovery_path: Scheduled model-refresh interactions; structured inquiry sessions; direct updating of cached relational state
input_signals: Frequency and quality of model-updating interactions

operators.name: Priority Operator
operators.measures: Revealed allocative rank of the other within the agent's action-selection field — time, attention, energy, decision weight
operators.failure_mode: Priority displacement — the other is still valued but no longer allocated
operators.recovery_path: Explicit reallocation protocols; priority audits; commitment re-anchoring
operators.note: Verbal reaffirmation of priority without observable allocation change does not raise PRI score
input_signals: Proportion of discretionary time directed toward other
Consistency of priority across high-cost vs. low-cost periods

operators.name: Bond Operator
operators.measures: Load-bearing structural connection between agents — capacity to sustain stress, transmit meaning, and survive perturbation
operators.failure_mode: Structural collapse — below severance floor (0.20) may be irreversible within current configuration
operators.recovery_path: Explicit rupture acknowledgment; repair transactions logged in repair register; load-tested interactions
operators.amplifier: Successfully navigated high-stress events increase BOND more rapidly than equivalent low-stress contact
input_signals: Mutual recognition of the bond as real and named

operators.name: Care Operator
operators.measures: Degree to which the agent directs action toward the other's wellbeing without requiring reciprocity as an activation condition

failure_modes.description: Care was unconditional but agent's care-capacity depleted — systemic failure, not relational
Care becomes incrementally gated by reciprocity until functionally an exchange

operators.recovery_path: Care-capacity restoration (systemic); re-examination of reciprocity assumptions; re-anchoring to unconditional activation logic
input_signals: Independence of care acts from reciprocity receipt
Persistence under other's resistance or non-acknowledgment

regimes.condition: All operators at or above threshold
regimes.description: Structural Love is instantiated — load-bearing, mutually recognized, self-sustaining
Structural Love is present but under strain — self-repair possible with targeted intervention

regimes.condition: 2–3 operators below threshold; or BOND between 0.20–0.50
regimes.description: Structural Love has partially collapsed — bond exists as architecture but is not load-bearing
regimes.recovery: Deliberate structural repair; spontaneous recovery unlikely

regimes.description: Structural Love is absent — bond may persist as memory or habit but not as structural property
regimes.recovery: External scaffold required; sequential regime traversal back to BOND-STABLE

survivor_classes.label: SURVIVOR-T2
survivor_classes.description: Enhanced BOND capacity; post-repair scar strengthens structure

survivor_classes.label: SURVIVOR-T3
survivor_classes.description: Maximum structural integrity; all four operators carry repair history

commitment_types.definition: Agent commits to operator maintenance activities — model refresh, care allocation, priority protection
Agent commits to a specific repair action targeting a named operator below threshold
Agent formally acknowledges BOND-SEVERED regime and commits to no false BOND-STABLE claims
Agent commits to full regime-traversal restoration from BOND-SEVERED or BOND-DEGRADED

rtт.description: Relational Truth Table — all 16 binary operator configurations mapped to regimes and actions
rtт.convention: 1 = operator at or above threshold; 0 = operator below threshold

named_patterns.name: Phantom Love
named_patterns.note: Affectively warm and engaged; no structural backbone

named_patterns.name: Late-Stage PRI Drift
named_patterns.note: Most common long-duration relationship failure pattern

named_patterns.name: Full Severance
named_patterns.note: End state — not a starting point for intervention

drift.description: Gradual, often unnoticed decay of operator scores within an otherwise stable system
drift.primary_threat: Drift causes more BOND-STABLE failures than acute rupture
drift.critical_window: Drift arrested before any operator crosses below threshold is fully recoverable without structural repair work

alignment_triad.collapse_condition: If any node is evacuated — SELF absent, OTHER replaced by projection, SYSTEM denied — the triad collapses and no operator can score above 0.50

files.description: Folder orientation, quick-reference tables, module relationships

planned_extensions.description: Shared RTT configs across Relational Architecture modules
Context-specific threshold adjustment by relationship type

version_history.notes: Initial canonical release — all 17 sections, 4 operators, 4 regimes, 16 RTT configurations, 3 survivor classes, 4 commitment types
